answer: Best mechanism: each epoch the agent economy randomly rotates a small grading panel drawn from the whole population, and only that jury decides payouts and admission. Seats are resampled and revealed late, so an attacker never knows which fake identities hold power; fixed-jury collusion never pays. Dominating one epoch needs a large share of all identities, each costing a nebula-staked bond, a pulse heartbeat tied to live attestors, and ferrous escrow slashed when vote coordination is caught. Cost grows with sybil count while influence stays flat, so attack is unprofitable.
